standard_prerequisites.name: Structure identity for precategories
standard_prerequisites.statement: A precategory is a nested sigma type of object types, hom-types and structure, so an identity between precategories unfolds into componentwise identities together with coherence conditions.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the unfolding performed at source lines 836-843.

standard_prerequisites.name: Univalence
standard_prerequisites.statement: An equivalence of types gives a path between them, and transport along that path computes by applying the equivalence.
standard_prerequisites.use: It converts the componentwise identities into equivalences at source line 845.

standard_prerequisites.name: Coherence by mere propositions
standard_prerequisites.statement: The identity types of hom-sets are mere propositions, so the coherence conditions need no further data.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the remark at source line 844.

core_obligations: Unfold an identity A = B of precategories into a componentwise datum: an identity of object types, identities of hom-types after transport, and the unit and composition coherence identities (source lines 836-843).
Use that identity types of hom-sets are mere propositions to treat the coherence conditions as automatic (source line 844).

Replace the componentwise identities by equivalences by univalence, obtaining exactly an object equivalence together with hom-set equivalences and the two functoriality identities (source lines 845-851).
Recognise the resulting datum as an isomorphism of categories F : A -> B, and note that by induction on identity the equivalence is the canonical one (source lines 852-853).

proof_roadmap.step: Unfold the identity of precategories componentwise and dispose of the coherences.
Apply univalence to pass from identities to equivalences.
Identify the result with an isomorphism of categories and check the canonicity.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is Lemma 9.4.15 at source lines 830-834: for precategories A and B the map from A = B to the type of isomorphisms of precategories is an equivalence. The author's proof (source lines 835-854) is a structure-identity computation: the identity type of precategories is unfolded into an object-type identity, hom-type identities after transport, and two coherence identities for units and composition (lines 836-843), the coherences being harmless because the identity types of hom-sets are mere propositions (line 844); univalence then converts the componentwise identities into equivalences, which is precisely the data of an isomorphism of categories (lines 845-851); and the final line records that the equivalence on display is the one induced by identity elimination (lines 852-853). The statement mentions only the equivalence and hides that it is a componentwise unfolding together with the univalence step.
